# Purpose

Notebooks 03-05 told us **how likely a driver is to say yes** to each offer. This notebook turns that into **net 12-month dollars after cost**, the One Number for Milestone 2.

```
value of one offer  =  p x r x (1 - phi) x f   -   (1 - p) x c
                       \_________________/       \_________/
                       fee we actually earn      cost of an unwanted offer
```

| Symbol | Meaning | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| p | probability the driver says yes (stated acceptance) | our model, notebook 05 |
| r | share of "yes" answers that become real redemptions | **ledger** |
| f | fee Momentum earns per redemption, by category | **ledger** |
| phi | share of redemptions that would have happened anyway (non-incremental) | **ledger** |
| c | cost of an unwanted offer = switch-off probability x 12-month driver value | **ledger** |

An offer is worth launching when p is above the **break-even acceptance** `p* = c / (r x (1 - phi) x f + c)`.

**How to use this notebook.** The only cell you edit is the **ledger in section 0**. It ships with clearly marked *placeholder* numbers so every chart runs. Replace a row's numbers and change its `source` from `PLACEHOLDER` to the real citation, and that row counts as *sourced*. Until **every** row is sourced, the notebook stays in **DEMO mode**: every figure is stamped DEMO, files are saved with a `DEMO_` prefix, and nothing is written under the final names. Demo output must never go into the memo or video.

# 0. The Assumption Ledger: fill in here

This is the **one cell** to edit. One row per input. For each: a `low`, `base` and `high` value, and a `source` (a link, report name or a one-line reasoned argument). Keep `category` as it is.

- `fee_per_redemption`: dollars Momentum earns when one coupon is redeemed, **per category**. Typically commission % x average ticket (for example 15% x $14 = $2.10). Show the working in `source`.
- `redemption_share`: of drivers who *say yes* in the survey, the share who really redeem. Delivered-coupon redemption rates (5-10%) must be divided by our ~57% stated acceptance first.
- `switch_off_prob`: probability that **one unwanted offer** makes a driver turn Momentum offers off for good.
- `driver_value_12m`: dollars of fees a driver would generate over 12 months if they keep offers on.
- `offers_per_driver_month`, `n_drivers`: volume.
- `implementation_cost`: one-off cost over the 12 months, in dollars.
- `non_incremental_share`: share of redemptions that would have happened without the offer (0 to 1).

```{r}
#| label: ledger
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

# ============================================================================
#  ASSUMPTION LEDGER  -  EDIT THIS CELL ONLY
#  Replace the numbers, then replace "PLACEHOLDER" in `source` with the real source.
#  A row is treated as real only when its source no longer starts with PLACEHOLDER.
#  Leave `low`/`high` as NA if you have no range (the sensitivity then uses +/-50% of base).
# ============================================================================
ledger <- tribble(
  ~input,                     ~category,                 ~unit,                        ~low,   ~base,   ~high,  ~source,
  # --- fee per redemption, by category (owner: Kai) -------------------------
  "fee_per_redemption",       "Restaurant (under $20)",  "$ per redeemed coupon",       1.20,    2.00,    3.00, "PLACEHOLDER",
  "fee_per_redemption",       "Coffee House",            "$ per redeemed coupon",       0.30,    0.60,    1.00, "PLACEHOLDER",
  "fee_per_redemption",       "Take-away",               "$ per redeemed coupon",       0.80,    1.50,    2.50, "PLACEHOLDER",
  "fee_per_redemption",       "Bar",                     "$ per redeemed coupon",       1.50,    3.00,    5.00, "PLACEHOLDER",
  "fee_per_redemption",       "Restaurant ($20-50)",     "$ per redeemed coupon",       2.50,    4.50,    7.00, "PLACEHOLDER",
  # --- behaviour (owner: Varinder) ------------------------------------------
  "redemption_share",         NA,                        "share of 'yes' that redeem",  0.08,    0.12,    0.18, "PLACEHOLDER",
  "switch_off_prob",          NA,                        "prob. per unwanted offer",    0.002,   0.005,   0.010, "PLACEHOLDER",
  "driver_value_12m",         NA,                        "$ fees per driver, 12 mo",   20,      40,      80,    "PLACEHOLDER",
  "non_incremental_share",    NA,                        "share of redemptions (0-1)",  0.20,    0.35,    0.50, "PLACEHOLDER",
  # --- scale and cost (owner: Kai) ------------------------------------------
  "offers_per_driver_month",  NA,                        "offers per driver per month", 5,       10,      20,   "PLACEHOLDER",
  "n_drivers",                NA,                        "drivers on the platform",     10000,   20000,   40000, "PLACEHOLDER",
  "implementation_cost",      NA,                        "$ over 12 months",            100000,  150000,  300000, "PLACEHOLDER"
)

# Small settings (usually leave as they are)
HEADLINE   <- "cell"   # policy behind the One Number: "cell" (recommended), "category", or "row"
MIN_CELL_N <- 30       # cells with fewer survey rows are never launched (too thin to trust)
PILOT_ALPHA <- 0.05; PILOT_POWER <- 0.80; PILOT_MARGIN <- 0.03   # pilot design: test size, power, +/- margin on r
B_BOOT     <- 2000     # bootstrap resamples
```

# 1. Check the ledger

```{r}
#| label: checks
CATS <- c("Restaurant (under $20)", "Coffee House", "Take-away", "Bar", "Restaurant ($20-50)")
NEEDED <- c("redemption_share", "switch_off_prob", "driver_value_12m", "non_incremental_share",
            "offers_per_driver_month", "n_drivers", "implementation_cost")

# structure
stopifnot(setequal(ledger$category[ledger$input == "fee_per_redemption"], CATS))
stopifnot(all(NEEDED %in% ledger$input), !anyDuplicated(ledger[c("input", "category")]))
stopifnot(HEADLINE %in% c("cell", "category", "row"))
if (anyNA(ledger$base)) stop("Every row needs a base value: ", paste(ledger$input[is.na(ledger$base)], collapse = ", "))

# fill a missing low/high with +/-50% of base, and remember we did
ledger <- ledger |>
  mutate(range_assumed = is.na(low) | is.na(high),
         low  = coalesce(low,  base * 0.5),
         high = coalesce(high, base * 1.5))
stopifnot(all(ledger$low <= ledger$base & ledger$base <= ledger$high))
stopifnot(all(ledger$base[ledger$input %in% c("redemption_share", "switch_off_prob", "non_incremental_share")] <= 1))
stopifnot(all(ledger$base >= 0))

# which rows are real?
ledger <- ledger |>
  mutate(sourced = !str_detect(source, regex("^\\s*PLACEHOLDER", ignore_case = TRUE)))
LEDGER_READY <- all(ledger$sourced)
MODE  <- if (LEDGER_READY) "FINAL" else "DEMO"
STAMP <- if (LEDGER_READY) NULL else "DEMO placeholder values - not for the memo or video"
PFX   <- if (LEDGER_READY) "" else "DEMO_"

status <- ledger |>
  transmute(input, category = coalesce(category, ""),
            base = format(base, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE, trim = TRUE),
            status = if_else(sourced, "sourced", "PLACEHOLDER"),
            range = if_else(range_assumed, "range assumed +/-50%", ""))
print(as.data.frame(status), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nMODE:", MODE, "-", sum(ledger$sourced), "of", nrow(ledger), "ledger rows sourced\n")

# the ledger as a lookup the rest of the notebook uses
par_from <- function(col = "base") {
  g <- function(nm) ledger[[col]][ledger$input == nm]
  fee <- ledger |> filter(input == "fee_per_redemption")
  list(fee = setNames(fee[[col]], fee$category)[CATS],
       r = g("redemption_share"), s = g("switch_off_prob"), V = g("driver_value_12m"),
       phi = g("non_incremental_share"), offers_pm = g("offers_per_driver_month"),
       drivers = g("n_drivers"), impl = g("implementation_cost"))
}
par0 <- par_from("base")

# plotting + saving helpers (same look as notebooks 04 and 05)
blue <- "#2a78d6"; red <- "#e34948"; grey <- "#b8b6ae"
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.title.position = "plot",
                  plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")))
wrap <- function(x, w = 55) stringr::str_wrap(x, w)
dir.create("../outputs/figures", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("../outputs/tables",  showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
save_fig <- function(p, name, w = 9, h = 5) {
  ggsave(file.path("../outputs/figures", paste0(PFX, name, ".png")), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 200, bg = "white")
  p
}
save_tbl <- function(x, name) write_csv(x, file.path("../outputs/tables", paste0(PFX, name, ".csv")))
# short dollar labels: $850, $12k, $1.24M (negatives get a minus sign)
usd <- function(x) {
  a <- round(abs(x))
  body <- ifelse(a >= 1e6, paste0(formatC(a / 1e6, format = "f", digits = 2), "M"),
          ifelse(a >= 1e3, paste0(formatC(a / 1e3, format = "f", digits = 0), "k"),
                           formatC(a, format = "f", digits = 0)))
  ifelse(is.na(x), NA_character_, paste0(ifelse(x < 0, "-", ""), "$", body))
}
usd2 <- label_dollar(accuracy = 0.01)
```

# 2. Load the model outputs from notebook 05

The honest predictions in `coupon_scored.rds` are out-of-fold for training respondents and test-set predictions for test respondents, so no row is scored by a model that saw it. We **decide** with the predicted acceptance and **value** with what drivers actually said.

```{r}
#| label: load
sc <- read_rds("../data/processed/coupon_scored.rds") |>
  transmute(respondent_id, coupon = as.character(coupon), cell, context = as.character(context),
            Y, p = p_logit)

cell_csv <- read_csv("../outputs/tables/cell_predictions.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# one row per cell
meta <- sc |> distinct(cell, coupon, context) |> arrange(coupon, context)
stopifnot(nrow(meta) == nrow(cell_csv))

# respondent x cell matrices, so a bootstrap is a fast matrix product
resp  <- sort(unique(sc$respondent_id))
ri <- match(sc$respondent_id, resp); ci <- match(sc$cell, meta$cell)
tab <- function(v) { M <- matrix(0, length(resp), nrow(meta)); for (i in seq_along(v)) M[ri[i], ci[i]] <- M[ri[i], ci[i]] + v[i]; M }
Nm <- tab(rep(1, nrow(sc))); Pm <- tab(sc$p); Sm <- tab(sc$Y)

make_cells <- function(n, sp, sy) {
  meta |> mutate(n = n, sp = sp, sy = sy,
                 p_dec = if_else(n > 0, sp / n, NA_real_),    # predicted acceptance: used to decide
                 p_val = if_else(n > 0, sy / n, NA_real_),    # observed acceptance: used to value
                 w = n / sum(n), thin = n < MIN_CELL_N)
}
cells0 <- make_cells(colSums(Nm), colSums(Pm), colSums(Sm))

# integrity check against the table saved by notebook 05
chk <- cells0 |> inner_join(cell_csv, by = "cell")
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$p_dec - chk$predicted)) < 1e-9, max(abs(chk$p_val - chk$observed)) < 1e-9)

cat("Survey rows:", comma(nrow(sc)), "| respondents:", length(resp), "| cells:", nrow(cells0),
    "| thin cells (never launched):", sum(cells0$thin), "\n")
cat("Overall stated acceptance:", percent(mean(sc$Y), accuracy = 0.1), "\n")
```

**Volume assumption.** Annual offers are spread over cells in proportion to how often each cell appears in the survey. The survey design is not the real mix of what Momentum would send, so this is an assumption to state in the ledger discussion.

# 3. Break-even acceptance per category

An offer in this category should launch only if its predicted acceptance clears `p*`.

```{r}
#| label: breakeven
pstar <- function(par) {
  cu <- par$s * par$V
  gain <- par$r * (1 - par$phi) * par$fee
  cu / (gain + cu)
}

# pessimistic / optimistic: each input at whichever end of its range is worse / better for us
higher_is_better <- c(fee = TRUE, r = TRUE, s = FALSE, V = FALSE, phi = FALSE,
                      offers_pm = TRUE, drivers = TRUE, impl = FALSE)
par_case <- function(better = TRUE) {
  lo <- par_from("low"); hi <- par_from("high")
  pick <- function(k) if (higher_is_better[[k]] == better) hi[[k]] else lo[[k]]
  setNames(lapply(names(higher_is_better), pick), names(higher_is_better))
}
par_pess <- par_case(FALSE); par_opt <- par_case(TRUE)

be <- tibble(coupon = CATS,
             fee = par0$fee,
             `break-even, pessimistic` = pstar(par_pess),
             `break-even, base`        = pstar(par0),
             `break-even, optimistic`  = pstar(par_opt)) |>
  left_join(cells0 |> filter(!thin) |>
              group_by(coupon) |>
              summarise(`category acceptance` = sum(sy) / sum(n)), by = "coupon") |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("break-even"), ~ pmin(.x, 1)))
cat("Cost of one unwanted offer, base:", usd2(par0$s * par0$V), "\n\n")
print(be |> mutate(fee = usd2(fee), across(where(is.numeric), ~ percent(.x, accuracy = 1))) |> as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)
save_tbl(be, "06_breakeven")
```

A break-even above 100% means the category cannot pay for itself at any acceptance level under that scenario.

# 4. Net value per cell and the launch map

```{r}
#| label: policies-fn
# Value of every policy for a given parameter set and cell table
cell_policy <- function(par, cells) {
  cu <- par$s * par$V
  cells |>
    mutate(fee = par$fee[coupon],
           gain = par$r * (1 - par$phi) * fee,
           p_star = cu / (gain + cu),
           offers = w * par$offers_pm * 12 * par$drivers,
           v_offer = replace_na(p_val * gain - (1 - p_val) * cu, 0),
           if_sent = offers * v_offer,                       # annual $ if we send this cell
           launch_cell = !thin & !is.na(p_dec) & p_dec >= p_star) |>
    group_by(coupon) |>
    mutate(cat_p = sum(sp) / sum(n), launch_cat = cat_p >= p_star) |>
    ungroup()
}

# Row-level targeting: use each offer's own predicted acceptance (this uses habit match)
row_policy <- function(par, rows = sc) {
  cu <- par$s * par$V
  gain <- par$r * (1 - par$phi) * par$fee[rows$coupon]
  ps <- cu / (gain + cu)
  launch <- rows$p >= ps
  off <- par$offers_pm * 12 * par$drivers / nrow(rows)
  list(launch = launch, per_row = launch * (rows$Y * gain - (1 - rows$Y) * cu) * off)
}

cell_values <- function(par, cells) {          # the three policies that work on cells
  cp <- cell_policy(par, cells)
  c(`Send every offer`              = sum(cp$if_sent) - par$impl,
    `Launch whole categories`       = sum(cp$if_sent[cp$launch_cat]) - par$impl,
    `Launch cells above break-even` = sum(cp$if_sent[cp$launch_cell]) - par$impl)
}
policy_values <- function(par, cells, rows = sc) {
  c(cell_values(par, cells),
    `Target each offer (needs driver habit data)` = sum(row_policy(par, rows)$per_row) - par$impl)
}
HEAD_NAME <- c(cell = "Launch cells above break-even", category = "Launch whole categories",
               row = "Target each offer (needs driver habit data)")[[HEADLINE]]

cp0 <- cell_policy(par0, cells0)
cat("Cells launched (headline = cell rule):", sum(cp0$launch_cell), "of", nrow(cp0),
    "| thin cells skipped:", sum(cp0$thin), "\n")
```

"Target each offer" is the **upside if Momentum can see a driver's habit** (it uses the habit-match feature). We report it as an upside, not as the One Number, unless the team can show Momentum has that data.

# 6. Sensitivity: which assumption moves the answer?

Each ledger input is moved to its `low` and then its `high`, everything else held at base, and the **launch rule is re-optimised** each time. Fees move together across categories.

```{r}
#| label: tornado
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
base_net <- policy_values(par0, cells0)[[HEAD_NAME]]
labels <- c(fee = "Fee per redemption (all categories)", r = "Redemption share",
            s = "Switch-off probability", V = "12-month driver value",
            phi = "Non-incremental share", offers_pm = "Offers per driver per month",
            drivers = "Number of drivers", impl = "Implementation cost")
base_launch <- cp0$launch_cell

run_one <- function(key, col) {
  par <- par0; par[[key]] <- par_from(col)[[key]]
  cp <- cell_policy(par, cells0)
  tibble(net = policy_values(par, cells0)[[HEAD_NAME]], flips = sum(cp$launch_cell != base_launch))
}
tor <- map_dfr(names(labels), \(k) {
  lo <- run_one(k, "low"); hi <- run_one(k, "high")
  tibble(key = k, input = labels[[k]], net_low = lo$net, net_high = hi$net,
         flips_low = lo$flips, flips_high = hi$flips)
}) |>
  mutate(swing = abs(net_high - net_low)) |>
  arrange(desc(swing))
print(tor |> transmute(input, `at low` = usd(net_low), `at high` = usd(net_high),
                       `cells flipping (low/high)` = paste(flips_low, "/", flips_high)) |> as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)

p <- tor |>
  mutate(input = factor(input, rev(input))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(net_low, net_high), names_to = "end", values_to = "net") |>
  mutate(end = recode(end, net_low = "input at low", net_high = "input at high")) |>
  ggplot(aes(net, input)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = base_net, colour = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_segment(data = tor |> mutate(input = factor(input, rev(input))),
               aes(x = net_low, xend = net_high, y = input, yend = input), colour = grey, linewidth = 5) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = end), size = 3.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`input at low` = red, `input at high` = blue), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = usd) +
  labs(title = wrap("What moves the One Number: each input across its ledger range"),
       subtitle = paste0("Black line = base case (", usd(base_net), "). Dotted line = break-even ($0)."),
       x = "Net 12-month dollars", y = NULL, caption = STAMP) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
save_fig(p, "06_04_tornado", 9, 5)
save_tbl(tor |> select(-key), "06_tornado")
```

# 7. Uncertainty from the survey sample

We resample **respondents** (not rows, because each person answered many offers), re-decide the launch map each time and recompute the net dollars. This captures survey sampling noise. It does **not** cover ledger uncertainty; the tornado does.

```{r}
#| label: bootstrap
set.seed(445)
row0 <- row_policy(par0)
resp_row_val <- as.numeric(tapply(row0$per_row, factor(sc$respondent_id, resp), sum)); resp_row_val[is.na(resp_row_val)] <- 0

rows_per_resp <- rowSums(Nm)
N0 <- nrow(sc)
pol_names <- names(policy_values(par0, cells0))

boot <- map_dfr(seq_len(B_BOOT), \(b) {
  wts <- tabulate(sample.int(length(resp), replace = TRUE), nbins = length(resp))
  cl  <- make_cells(drop(wts %*% Nm), drop(wts %*% Pm), drop(wts %*% Sm))
  cv  <- cell_values(par0, cl)
  # row policy: launch flags depend only on the ledger, so just re-weight respondents
  rv  <- sum(wts * resp_row_val) * N0 / sum(wts * rows_per_resp) - par0$impl
  as_tibble_row(setNames(c(b, cv, rv), c("b", pol_names)))
})

ci <- boot |> select(-b) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "policy", values_to = "net") |>
  group_by(policy) |>
  summarise(lo = quantile(net, 0.025), hi = quantile(net, 0.975), p_positive = mean(net > 0), .groups = "drop")
pol <- pol |> select(policy, net, headline) |> left_join(ci, by = "policy")
print(pol |> transmute(policy, net = usd(net), `95% interval` = paste(usd(lo), "to", usd(hi)),
                       `chance net > $0` = percent(p_positive, accuracy = 1)) |> as.data.frame(), row.names = FALSE)

head_ci <- pol |> filter(headline)
p <- boot |>
  ggplot(aes(.data[[HEAD_NAME]])) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = blue, colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = head_ci$net, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(head_ci$lo, head_ci$hi), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = red) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = usd) +
  labs(title = wrap("If we had surveyed different drivers, the One Number would land here"),
       subtitle = paste0("Black = base (", usd(head_ci$net), "). Dashed = 95% interval. Red = break-even."),
       x = "Net 12-month dollars", y = "Resamples", caption = STAMP)
save_fig(p, "06_05_bootstrap", 9, 4.5)
save_tbl(pol, "06_policies")
```

# 9. Pilot design: how we would find out for real

The model uses **stated** acceptance, and the ledger numbers are assumptions. A pilot with a **no-offer control group** replaces the assumptions with measurements. The sizes below come straight from the ledger: offers in the launched cells redeem at `q = acceptance x redemption share`, and the control group would redeem at `phi x q` anyway.

```{r}
#| label: pilot
if (nrow(launched) == 0) {
  cat("No cell launches under the base ledger, so there is nothing to pilot. Check the ledger.\n")
} else {
  q <- with(launched, sum(offers * p_val * par0$r) / sum(offers))                  # redemption per offer sent
  pbar <- with(launched, sum(offers * p_val) / sum(offers))
  fbar <- with(launched, sum(offers * fee) / sum(offers))
  pw   <- power.prop.test(p1 = max(par0$phi, 0.01) * q, p2 = q, sig.level = PILOT_ALPHA, power = PILOT_POWER)
  n_arm <- ceiling(pw$n)
  zz <- qnorm(1 - PILOT_ALPHA / 2)
  n_yes <- ceiling(zz^2 * par0$r * (1 - par0$r) / PILOT_MARGIN^2)
  delta_base <- (1 - par0$phi) * q                                                 # incremental redemptions per offer
  # incremental redemptions per offer needed to cover unwanted-offer cost AND the fixed implementation cost
  delta_be   <- ((1 - pbar) * par0$s * par0$V + par0$impl / sum(launched$offers)) / fbar
  pilot <- tribble(
    ~item, ~value,
    "Redemption rate per offer sent, treatment (base)",           percent(q, accuracy = 0.1),
    "Redemption rate per offer sent, control if phi is right",    percent(par0$phi * q, accuracy = 0.1),
    "Offers needed per arm to tell the two apart",                comma(n_arm),
    "Driver-months per arm at planned offer volume",              comma(ceiling(n_arm / par0$offers_pm)),
    paste0("Accepted offers needed to pin the redemption share to +/-", percent(PILOT_MARGIN, accuracy = 1)), comma(n_yes),
    "Incremental redemptions per offer we expect (base)",         percent(delta_base, accuracy = 0.1),
    "Incremental redemptions per offer needed to break even (incl. implementation cost)", percent(delta_be, accuracy = 0.1))
  print(as.data.frame(pilot), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nDecision rule: scale up if the measured treatment-minus-control redemption rate per offer is at least",
      percent(delta_be, accuracy = 0.1), "and the switch-off rate in the treatment arm is no higher than the ledger assumes",
      percent(par0$s, accuracy = 0.1), "per unwanted offer. Otherwise stop or retarget.\n")
  save_tbl(pilot, "06_pilot")
}
```
